title: map, filter, reduce, compactMap, flatMap
summary: Higher-order functions take a closure and apply it to every element, so you describe what you want instead of writing loops.
body: **In simple words:** Instead of writing a `for` loop with a temporary array, you say: "give me the names" (`map`), "only adults" (`filter`), "add them up" (`reduce`).

**The five you must know:** `map` transforms each element (same count). `filter` keeps elements that pass a test. `reduce` combines all elements into one value. `compactMap` transforms and drops `nil` results. `flatMap` transforms each element into an array and joins all arrays into one.
**Performance:** each call creates a new array. For long chains on big data, use `.lazy` so elements flow through the chain one at a time without intermediate arrays.
keyPoints: `map` = transform, `filter` = keep some, `reduce` = combine into one, `compactMap` = transform and drop nils, `flatMap` = flatten nested arrays.
They make intent clear and avoid mutable temp variables.
Use `.lazy` for long chains or when you only need the first few results.
`reduce(into:)` is faster than `reduce` for building arrays or dictionaries because it mutates in place.

code.caption: Common chains
code.text:
let users = [User(name: "Asha", age: 31), User(name: "Ravi", age: 17)]

let names  = users.map(\.name)                         // ["Asha", "Ravi"]
let adults = users.filter { $0.age >= 18 }              // [Asha]
let total  = users.reduce(0) { $0 + $1.age }            // 48
let ids    = ["1", "x", "3"].compactMap(Int.init)       // [1, 3]
let tags   = posts.flatMap(\.tags)                      // all tags in one array
let byAge  = Dictionary(grouping: users) { $0.age >= 18 ? "adult" : "minor" }

let firstBig = hugeArray.lazy.map(expensive).first { $0 > 100 }  // stops early

mistakes: Using `flatMap` to drop nils (old Swift) - that is `compactMap` now.
Using `forEach` when you need to `return`/`break` early - use a `for` loop.
followups: **Difference between `map` and `compactMap`?** `compactMap` removes `nil` results and unwraps the rest.
**Is `map` faster than a for loop?** About the same; choose for readability. `.lazy` avoids extra arrays.
